note_sections.locator: 1. Motivation：先判断研究计划是否值得做

source_visuals.label: FARS pipeline: research direction, ideation, planning, experiment, writing, paper; all stages share one workspace
source_visuals.rationale: FARS pipeline is motivation background; its ideation bottleneck is retained in Motivation without republishing this unlicensed drawing.

source_visuals.label: Evaluation signals on an idea’s timeline. When the idea is proposed, before any experiment: expert ratings [9][10] and novelty checks [14]. After experiments: experimental outcomes [15] and hypothesis verification [16][17]. At publication: matching the published paper [5–8] and acceptance or reviews [11–13]. Months to years later: citations and awards [18][19]. Earlier signals are noisy or partial; complete signals arrive only after the fact. Research taste means predicting, at the moment an idea is proposed, what the community will say later
source_visuals.rationale: Signal timeline is represented by the related-work comparison organized by input/output/label; image is not independently licensed.

source_visuals.label: Envisioned ideation loop: a Seeder generates proposals, a Filter removes invalid ones, a pairwise Ranker updates Elo scores in the candidate pool, an Evolver revises the top proposals, and the best one is delivered
source_visuals.rationale: Seeder/Filter/Elo/Evolver is an envisioned future loop, not an executed mechanism or reported gain; retain the project scope rather than making it the main method.

source_visuals.label: K_t is the work on one research question published before cutoff t. Human proposals from the next 31 days build on the same K_t, and an AI proposal generated at t can only draw on K_t. A pairwise ranker compares two human proposals and is checked against later citations (calibration), then compares the AI proposal with every human proposal in the cohort (ideation)
source_visuals.rationale: Use licensed repository overview to teach cohort generation and separate calibration/ideation; do not copy the blog-specific drawing.

source_visuals.label: Left: the corpus of 35,505 papers splits level by level until every leaf holds 10 to 50 papers. Research-question granularity is set by size: the highest node whose subtree holds at most 150 papers is a topic, itself a broader research question, and each leaf is a finer one. Right: one topic on a timeline cut into 31-day windows; each window is a cohort. Each leaf alone is sparse within a window, while the topic as a whole gives enough papers
source_visuals.rationale: Use licensed repository taxonomy plus explicit actual counts; the blog figure adds cohort timeline now taught in §3.1.

source_visuals.label: Paper to proposal: a paper’s content is sorted into plan, prior knowledge, and results; results are removed, findings are rewritten as hypotheses, and the rest goes into a seven-section proposal template with results marked TBD
source_visuals.rationale: Paper-to-proposal information boundary and all seven sections are taught in §3.2; no need to republish animation artwork.
